name: ropensci/patentsview
what_it_holds: R client (ropensci-vetted, 39 stars, active as of Jul 2026) to the free PatentsView API (USPTO bulk patent data). No data committed; wraps query/fieldsets/subscore endpoints for patent search, assignees, inventors, CPC classes. Could pull Airbnb's own patent filings (assignee='Airbnb') and counts over time as a product-development-pace proxy.
why_useful: Addresses gap #15 (patents/trademarks as company-structure/product-launch signal) — patent filing counts/timing can be a lagging proxy for feature roadmap and M&A-adjacent R&D. Free API, no key required in most PatentsView modes.
themes: Product-launch monitors: certificate transparency (crt.sh) tooling, app release-notes scrapers, Wayback diff tools, help-center change monitors, trademark/patent (USPTO, PatentsView) clients
why_all: Addresses gap #15 (patents/trademarks as company-structure/product-launch signal) — patent filing counts/timing can be a lagging proxy for feature roadmap and M&A-adjacent R&D. Free API, no key required in most PatentsView modes.

Could pull Airbnb's (assignee-disambiguated) patent grant history and technology-category tags over time as a slow-moving product-roadmap signal (gap #15) -- R rather than Python, but PatentsView's disambiguated assignee IDs are the main value-add over raw USPTO bulk data.

name: patent_client
what_it_holds: Archived (April 2026) Python ORM-style unified client covering USPTO Patent Examination Data, Open Data Portal, Global Dossier, Patent Assignments, PTAB, Patent Public Search, Bulk Data Storage, plus EPO Inpadoc. Pandas-integrated, Pydantic v2 models. 632 commits, 128 stars, Apache 2.0. Note: archived/read-only, successor is an AI-agent-focused rewrite not evaluated here.
why_useful: One client covers multiple USPTO patent/assignment endpoints, so it could pull Airbnb's (and Vacasa/Sonder/Booking's) patent filing and assignment history as a very-low-frequency but genuine leading indicator of product roadmap (gap #15). Being archived means it may need patching for current USPTO API changes.

name: pylegiscan
what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the LegiScan API, which covers bill text, status, votes, and sponsors for all 50 US state legislatures plus Congress. Not STR-specific and holds no committed dataset, but is a working, well-starred (23 stars) way to programmatically pull STR-related bills (keyword search e.g. 'short-term rental', 'vacation rental') across every state legislature in one client.
why_useful: Directly matches gap #12's 'Legistar/LegiScan tooling' call-out -- a keyword search for 'short-term rental' across state legislatures could feed a US STR-ordinance/bill tracker; requires a free LegiScan API key.
last_activity: small repo, 7 commits, no visible recent activity
time_coverage: current LegiScan bill data (not a static historical file)
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: Directly matches gap #12's 'Legistar/LegiScan tooling' call-out -- a keyword search for 'short-term rental' across state legislatures could feed a US STR-ordinance/bill tracker; requires a free LegiScan API key.

Turns gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers) into a pullable, nationwide bill-tracking method rather than a one-city hand-built database — could build a state-by-state STR-restriction bill count/status series as a regulatory-intensity index.

name: CodeForBc/airbnb-regulation
what_it_holds: Code for BC civic-tech project building a pipeline to flag Airbnb listings in British Columbia that violate provincial short-term-rental rules: a scraping/data-ingestion module plus a rules-based compliance classifier, output to a Grafana dashboard. No committed regulation text or listing dataset in the repo itself — it is a live scrape+rules method, not a stored dataset.
why_useful: A working method for detecting non-compliant STR listings against a specific regulatory regime (BC's 2024 provincial STR restrictions); could be adapted as a template for measuring de-facto STR supply compression under new rules elsewhere, but requires running a scraper against Airbnb (a ToS decision, not to be run).
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)
why_all: A working method for detecting non-compliant STR listings against a specific regulatory regime (BC's 2024 provincial STR restrictions); could be adapted as a template for measuring de-facto STR supply compression under new rules elsewhere, but requires running a scraper against Airbnb (a ToS decision, not to be run).

A working method for turning STR registration/compliance policy into a quantifiable violation rate, relevant to gap #12 (city/provincial STR registration datasets). Note: it scrapes airbnb.com directly, so per repo rules this is catalogued as a method only and must not be run without a human ToS decision.
